3) Recurrent erythema nodosum — Common cause of tender nodules on lower legs; distribution on face/neck is atypical and the 3-year chronicity is unusual, but recurrent EN remains possible.
4) Erythema induratum (nodular vasculitis) — Chronic, painful nodules classically on calves that may ulcerate; associated with TB or other triggers.
5) Infectious panniculitis (atypical mycobacteria or deep fungal infection) — Chronic nodules that may be indolent and localized to skin/subcutis; consider when lesions persist for years.

Key reasons this is the differential: multiple chronic subcutaneous nodules in a woman of childbearing age with minimal systemic symptoms — favors non-infectious inflammatory panniculitides (sarcoidosis, lupus panniculitis, EN/induratum), with infectious causes and rarer neoplastic panniculitides less likely but included.

- Chest imaging (chest x-ray; consider chest CT if x-ray abnormal) to look for hilar adenopathy consistent with sarcoidosis.
- Basic labs: CBC, ESR and CRP.
- Autoimmune screen: ANA (and consider anti-dsDNA, complement) if lupus panniculitis suspected.
- TB testing (IGRA or PPD) if erythema induratum or mycobacterial infection suspected.
